Maya (AE): Hey team — ran the full end-to-end load test with PexelAI this morning. dropping raw results below.

Sam (SE): Cool — thanks. Summary first: steady-state throughput ~480 req/s, avg latency 110ms, p95 320ms, errors ~0.4% (mostly 429 during the first 3m spike).

Sam (SE): Test config: 200 concurrent users, ramp 0->200 over 3m, run 30m, payload includes 256-token prompts + embeddings call on the side.

Sam (SE): Command we used:
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m script.js --summary-export=pexelai-run.json
```

Sam (SE): Key snippet from the k6 summary (trimmed):
```
http_reqs...............: 864000  // total requests
iterations..............: 288000
vus_max.................: 200
http_req_duration.......: avg=110.3ms med=85.2ms p(95)=320.1ms p(99)=540.8ms
checks..................: 99.6% passed
errors..................: 0.4% (mostly 429)
```

Ben (SRE): I checked GPU-side metrics on Dedicated and saw one pod hit queue latency spikes during the ramp — gap introduced by autoscaler reacting ~45s late. After scale, tail latencies drop. Might tighten HPA config for canary.

Clara (Sales Ops): Pricing question from Ethan: what's the estimated monthly cost for this steady-state (480 rps) with 30% cache hit/kv savings? He wants a simple ballpark to compare against their current managed endpoint.

Maya (AE): Ethan, we're working the numbers but expected direction: with Redwood dedicated pricing + 30% cache, ballpark compute + infra for that workload is $Xk/month (I'll put a concrete after Ben and accounting). Also counsel about burst credit and committed slots.

Ethan (PexelAI): Appreciate the summary. Can you break down where 30% savings comes from? Also concerned about SLO if we see spikes — what's the recommended fallback model?

Sam (SE): 30% is from KV/prefix caching on repeated prompt prefixes + embeddings reuse. We observed token reuse across 40% of requests in the test dataset; effective per-token compute dropped. For spikes: recommended policy is auto-fallback to a smaller quantized variant (eg: redwood/quant-4x) + route to dedicated standby region. That keeps p95 bounded at cost of some quality.

Ben (SRE): Action item: tweak HPA minReplicas=3 -> 5 for this workload shape, reduce scaleDown stabilization to 30s. Also enable prewarm on canary rollout. I'll send the HPA diff in a sec.

Sam (SE): Also ran a short A/B with quantized variant for 10m: throughput +10% with avg latency +40ms but p95 improved during saturated periods because of higher concurrency CPU path. Raw compare:
```
variant,a_avg_ms,a_p95_ms
float32,110,320
quant4,150,290
```

Maya (AE): Great — can we convert this into a one-pager for the buyer? They want: run plan, key metrics, recommended infra config, cost ballpark, security note about token logging.

Clara (Sales Ops): I'll draft the summary. Need the cost input from finance for the dedicated commit tiers. @Ben can you provide expected GPU-hours and infra egress estimate for 480 rps steady-state (30% cache)?

Ben (SRE): Rough calc: 480 rps ~= 1.7M tokens/day (with their average prompt), GPU-hours ~18-22 GPUh/day (depends on quant), network egress ~1.5TB/month. I'll give a tighter number with logs.

Ethan (PexelAI): On security — our questionnaire shows question about customer data residency and KMS. Are there redwood private deployment options we can see in an NDA?

Maya (AE): Yes — Private (VPC/on-prem) is an option. I'll attach the SOC doc under NDA. For the POC we used hosted dedicated but we can spin a Private trial for their compliance team if needed.

deploy-bot: Deployment: canary-pexelai-load-test -> succeeded (commit abc123) :rocket:

Sam (SE): Follow-ups: 1) Ben to share HPA diff and exact GPU-hour calc, 2) Clara to assemble buyer one-pager and cost ballpark, 3) Maya to share SOC/KMS NDA link with Ethan.

Maya (AE): Timeline: aim to send the one-pager + cost by EOD tomorrow. Ben, can you get the HPA and GPU numbers by noon?

Ben (SRE): Yep — will post by 11:45.

Clara (Sales Ops): Drafting the one-pager now — will ping for any clarifications.

Ethan (PexelAI): Thanks all. This is helpful. Small ask: could you include a brief note on expected cold-start behavior for models after idle 15m? That impacts client retry logic.

Sam (SE): Cold-start: median cold-start for that model on Dedicated ~220ms additional to first-token latency; with prewarm policy it's ~30ms. We'll document recommended retry/backoff pattern.

Maya (AE): Perfect. Closing this thread when Clara posts the one-pager.

Clara (Sales Ops): Uploaded initial one-pager draft to the deal folder and linked in thread: https://redwood-internal/drive/pexelai/poc-onepager-v1. Feedback welcome. :thumbsup:
